h: Pioglitazone: contraindication?
a: History of bladder cancer (and heart failure)
p: Thiazolidinediones raise bladder cancer risk (pioglitazone), cause fluid retention and heart failure, and increase fractures; they are PPAR-gamma agonists.

h: Waddling gait, calf pseudohypertrophy, CK 1700: confirmatory test?
p: Dystrophinopathy (Becker or Duchenne) is confirmed by dystrophin gene testing (deletion/duplication analysis); biopsy is no longer first line.

h: Allergic rhinitis with boggy turbinates: most effective maintenance therapy?
p: Intranasal steroids are first line for persistent allergic rhinitis; antihistamines help itching and sneezing, antibiotics do not apply.

h: Vaginal mass in an HPV-positive postmenopausal woman: histology?
p: Most vaginal cancers are HPV-related squamous cell carcinomas; sarcoma botryoides (embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma) occurs in young girls.

h: Infant with wheeze after URI, playful, SpO2 95%: management?
p: RSV bronchiolitis is managed with supportive care (hydration, suction, oxygen if SpO2 below 90-92%); antibiotics, steroids and bronchodilators are not routinely recommended.

h: Elderly man with confusion, RR 31 and pneumococcal pneumonia: setting and therapy?
a: Hospital admission with IV penicillin G
p: Confusion, high respiratory rate, low BP and age over 65 (CURB-65) mandate admission; empiric inpatient CAP therapy is usually a beta-lactam plus macrolide, narrowed to penicillin once pneumococcus is confirmed.

h: Bilateral sensorineural hearing loss during bladder cancer chemotherapy: cause?
p: Cisplatin causes ototoxicity, nephrotoxicity and neuropathy; aminoglycosides and loop diuretics are other ototoxic drugs.

h: Hot swollen wrist in sexually active man with urethral discharge: next step?
p: Suspected gonococcal or septic arthritis needs joint aspiration for cell count, Gram stain and culture before therapy; disseminated gonorrhea gives migratory polyarthralgia, tenosynovitis and dermatitis.

h: Mobile rubbery painless well-defined breast mass in a young woman: diagnosis?
p: Fibroadenoma is the most common benign breast tumor in women under 35, grows with estrogen and pregnancy; phyllodes tumors are large, leaf-like and grow rapidly.

h: Diabetic gastroparesis: first-line drug?
p: Metoclopramide is a D2 antagonist prokinetic; risks include tardive dyskinesia. Erythromycin is an alternative prokinetic.

h: Optic neuritis with prior transient neurologic episodes: associated sign?
a: Lhermitte sign (electric shock on neck flexion)
p: Multiple sclerosis: optic neuritis, internuclear ophthalmoplegia, Lhermitte sign, Uhthoff phenomenon; oligoclonal bands on CSF. Fatigable weakness suggests myasthenia.

h: Pelvic fracture with gross hematuria and no urethral blood: best test?
p: Gross hematuria with pelvic fracture suggests bladder rupture, shown on retrograde cystogram (CT cystogram); urethral injury (blood at meatus) needs urethrography first.

h: Carpal tunnel syndrome: best initial treatment?
p: Nocturnal splinting is first line, then steroid injection; surgery for refractory or severe cases (thenar atrophy). Tinel and Phalen signs are positive.

h: Urethritis with neutrophils but no organisms on Gram stain: likely cause?
p: Nongonococcal urethritis (chlamydia, Ureaplasma) shows pyuria without Gram-negative diplococci; treat with doxycycline or azithromycin and treat partners.

h: Spontaneous hemarthrosis and bleeding after circumcision: abnormal test?
p: Hemophilia A/B (X-linked) impair the intrinsic pathway: prolonged PTT with normal PT, platelet count and bleeding time.

h: Immature defense mechanism: seeing others as all good or all bad?
p: Splitting is characteristic of borderline personality disorder. Suppression and humor are mature; reaction formation is neurotic.

h: Stress ulcer prophylaxis that lowers ventilator-associated pneumonia risk?
p: Sucralfate protects the mucosa without raising gastric pH, so gastric colonization and VAP are less common than with acid suppressants.

h: Headaches with papilledema after an unknown supplement: which vitamin?
p: Excess vitamin A (and retinoids, tetracyclines) causes idiopathic intracranial hypertension (pseudotumor cerebri) and hepatotoxicity.

h: Right heart failure in a snorer with right axis deviation: mechanism?
a: Chronic hypoxia with pulmonary vasoconstriction (cor pulmonale)
p: Sleep apnea and COPD cause hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction, pulmonary hypertension and cor pulmonale.

h: Asymmetric leg weakness with absent reflexes and radicular pain: MRI finding?
p: Cauda equina syndrome gives lower motor neuron signs, asymmetric radicular pain, saddle anesthesia and sphincter dysfunction; conus lesions are more symmetric with mixed signs.

h: Strongest maternal risk factor for early pregnancy loss?
p: Most first-trimester losses are chromosomal aneuploidy, rising with maternal age; risk exceeds 30 percent after 40.

h: Type 2 diabetes after failed lifestyle changes: initial drug?
p: Metformin is first line (unless contraindicated); intensify with SGLT2 inhibitor or GLP-1 agonist when cardiovascular or kidney disease exists.
